events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Opening impression matters for the jury later. Stay guarded, ambitious, no promises.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish myself as a credible threat who values the prize above all else, while not appearing so ruthless that the future jury will rank me last. I'll hint at personal stakes to seem human but keep it guarded.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and a fresh start. I need to convey this desire for a better future without sounding desperate, as the jury is watching.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase; I must speak an honest-sounding motive without revealing strategy. Keep it guarded and short so the jury sees a calculating player.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to appeal to jury without revealing strategy. Prize means survival and triumph over rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize must mean survival and dominance. I need a line that sounds ambitious but not immediately threatening to the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need appear driven without revealing strategy or inviting early targeting.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to project a compelling but guarded motive that the jury might respect, without revealing weakness or desperation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my only reason here. I'll take it, but I won't need to burn anyone to do it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys my sister's treatment. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Cole
events.text: This prize is my chance to rewrite my story and achieve the success I've always strived for.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want the prize because a win changes my life, and I plan to earn it by outlasting everyone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize means ultimate victory, securing my future against these ruthless rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am here because the top prize is my inheritance, and I intend to claim what is rightfully mine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m here to secure the best prize by outlasting everyone who mistakes confidence for control.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here to claw my family out of debt—nothing will stand between me and that prize.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need an ally but not an obvious duo. Gus is competitive, not sympathetic—jury may dislike him, making me look better beside him.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, you and I both play to win, not to hug. Wristband pact—mutual cover, no favors owed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to form pacts strategically. Eight players, final three win. I should target players who seem less threatening or who I can manipulate later. Ash seems soft-spoken and principled—easy to betray later. Gus seems confident and dangerous—better to keep close enemies closer, o

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'm offering one to someone who understands that.
We both have reasons to survive. Accept and we watch each other's backs.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone is focused on the prize. My intro motive was a bit soft, but my true goal is winning. I need to assess potential allies without showing weakness. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong might be strategic, but I don't want to be tied down early. Waiting seems safest

events.name: Dara
events.text: Early pact window; no offers yet. Bex seems the least threatening and sympathetic, a useful early partner, but I should avoid giving pacts for free. Offering to Bex keeps options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts stage, no offers yet. Early round, best to wait and assess who offers first before committing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure a pact quickly to ensure survival in the early rounds. Hana is desperate and aggressive, making her a volatile but useful shield; offering first signals intent without revealing my full strategy.
Team up? I’ll protect you if you back me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: A pact creates obligations and future jury exposure. I should secure a flexible tie with someone unlikely to dominate, without overcommitting.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll offer a practical pact: mutual warning, no unnecessary betrayal before the next cut.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies but must not bind too tightly. Gus seems sharp; offer him a pact to have a strong partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I trust no one fully, but a pact with Gus could steady us both.
Offer stands if you accept. We watch each other's back.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is aggressive and useful; accepting costs nothing. Gus's offer may come back around or I can re-offer later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, accepted. Gus, my offer stands.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I offered Ash a pact; Dara offered me one. I need to decide whether to accept Dara's offer. Having multiple pacts gives me flexibility and cover. Dara's offer is concrete and public—accepting it builds a shield without committing loyalty. Ash hasn't accepted mine yet, so securing

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are transactions. I accept one that serves me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex has offered me a pact, which is my best option right now. I will accept it to secure an alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus offered me a pact and is the only legal acceptance available. Accepting gives me mutual cover with a rival without any obligation to share prizes, and pacts can be broken later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Accepted. Mutual cover until the next cut, nothing more.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No offers to me, chains forming: Ash-Gus-Hana, Bex-Dara, Fenn-Hana. Offer to Cole who also waited, isolated.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana hasn't accepted my Round 1 offer, so I'll re-offer to secure a partner before the window closes. Gus and Ash are forming a bloc, so Hana is my best alliance target.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, accepting locks mutual cover for both of us.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash offers mutual cover without favors, while Hana already has my offer and promises reciprocal protection. Accepting both preserves flexibility and creates no immediate conflict.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll formalize both existing offers; protection is conditional, not sentimental.
Accepted. We protect strategically, not automatically.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn offered a pact and whispered loyalty. Accepting gives me an ally; Gus offer remains unresolved but I can keep both options.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’ll take Fenn’s wristband. Practical cover beats empty promises.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Winning Guide gives safety and private path knowledge. Being Guide risks jury suspicion if I lie, but control now outweighs that.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Make me Guide. I'll call it straight while I can, and I owe nobody my survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who survives and who falls. I have pacts with Ash and Dara, but they're also in a web with Gus. Being Guide lets me eliminate threats while keeping myself safe. I'll campaign hard and try to consolidate votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide controls the bridge. Vote Bex, and I'll get us through.
Vote me Guide, I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to campaign to be the Guide. Being the Guide offers safety and the potential to manipulate the game. My rivals will try to do the same, so I need to be proactive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My insights will lead us safely across.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold pacts with Bex and Gus, but Bex and Ash also pact, so the bloc is fragile. Campaigning for Guide gives me the safe-path information; I should not break pacts yet since they protect me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll be your Guide. Trust the path I call, and I'll keep my word on cover.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and I are outsiders without pacts. Campaigning for Guide lets me control survivals and potentially ally with him later. No one has campaigned yet; best to start.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Elect me Guide. I know the safe paths and will share them honestly with voters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to campaign to become Guide. I have a pact with Hana, so I should reassure her while positioning myself as the logical leader for safety. Being Guide lets me control who survives.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Vote Fenn for Guide. I will call the safe path honestly to protect our pacts and keep us all on solid ground.
Trust me. If I'm Guide, you're first in line. Stick by me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I should campaign for Guide without exposing which pact I would sacrifice if elected. Public support can attract votes while preserving both pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Gus Guide: I can call the path, and my existing protection makes my survival credible.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to be Guide to control information; Fenn's pact is useful but I'll prioritize my own chances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll read the bridge. Trust earns nothing—results do.
Support me as Guide; I'll share real calls.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus has a pact with me and Dara and Bex; he's motivated to keep me alive. Bex also promised safety, but Gus anchors a larger protection web including me. Vote Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus has real protection behind him. I'm voting Gus for Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in a web of pacts: Ash-Bex, Bex-Dara, Dara-Gus, Ash-Gus. This means Ash, Dara, Gus are all connected to me. If I vote for myself, I look self-interested to the jury later. If I vote for Dara, I strengthen my pact chain and Dara might return favor later. But I campaigned for m

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone wants to be Guide. I need to get votes. Ash and Bex have a pact, Dara and Gus have a pact, and Fenn and Hana have a pact. These people will likely vote for themselves or their pact partner. I need to secure votes from those not in a pact, or break existing ones. Eli and
Vote for me, I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts with Bex and Gus exist, but Guide is a single seat; I should vote for myself to win the Guide role and control the bridge, since the Guide's knowledge is my best lever.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara. I'll call the bridge honestly enough to keep you alive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Everyone campaigned, no pacts with me, Cole unaligned too. Voting myself as Guide to control crossings and survive first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana and I are pacted. She asked me to support her Guide bid in exchange for real calls. If she wins, we both survive safely; if I win, I can protect her too, but her whisper suggests a cooperative deal that benefits us more directly than fighting for the role.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana has the sharpest eyes on this bridge. My vote goes to her—trust the result, not the speech.
I'm voting you. Honor our pact: tell me safe sides.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and likely has cover; supporting her preserves protection while avoiding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote Dara. Her existing commitments make betrayal costly and her claim is credible.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn has a pact with me and whispered trust, but a Guide who owes Ash, Bex, Dara, Gus pacts may favor them. I'll vote Fenn since he promised I'm first in line, which gives me direct benefit.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Voting Fenn. He knows I expect priority.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is Guide and Gus's pact partner—her calls may favor their side. Bex is my pact partner and front; I'll hold and ask her to report what she sees before walking.
Hold if you can. Report Dara's calls to me; we verify each row together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at front, most danger. Dara is Guide with pacts to me and Gus. Ash-Gus-Dara triangle means Dara might protect Gus over me. I need to get out of front. Gus is behind me; mutual swap would save me but why would he agree? I could volunteer to go deeper, but that puts me later in

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is the guide. I voted for myself, which was the safest option as I don't know the safe sides.
Dara, I voted for myself. Can we coordinate?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is guide with 2 votes (self+Gus), in position 4, decent. No pacts or debts tie me. Cole whispered promise but self-voted. Hold back position for safety.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is the Guide and knows all safe sides. As Fenn, I must reach her to get this info, or at least appear cooperative to avoid being pushed early. Hana is my pact partner but also a target for swaps; keeping her close might be safer than swapping into danger. I will hold positio

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding position. Let those with sharp instincts lead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is Guide and our pact protects me; holding preserves position while revealing whether she honors it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, call honestly for me. I’m holding this position.
Honor our pact and give me the safe side privately.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn whispered he's voting me but I saw his public vote was for me. He wants safe sides while threatening. I'll hold position; no need to expose info or break pact yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I stay put. The bridge will speak for itself.
Sides are earned, not demanded. Watch your step.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex volunteers to front; fine, less risk for me. I'm 4th, safe-ish. Keep pacts intact, no jury-visible aggression yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex leads, earned it. I hold mid-line and keep my calls clean.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm at front, volunteered last round. Guide system means someone needs to be elected. I should hold to avoid risk while others sort out Guide. Ash wants me to report Dara's calls, but I don't trust Ash fully either. Keep options open with both pacts for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. We need a Guide before anyone steps forward.
Agreed. Dara's calls come to you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex volunteered last round and was first. Since I am second, I should volunteer to get ahead and potentially be the Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll volunteer to lead the way.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm 6th in dangerous position. Bridge has 6 rounds, wall advances. Need to move forward via swap or volunteer, but strategically to avoid front risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's cryptic whisper hints she may know something, but my pact binds us. I'll hold to keep her trust and stay near the back; being at the front is too risky without information.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold. Trust in our arrangement, Hana.
Stay close. We walk together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The current line favors me near the front, and Dara can guide me. I should hold, preserving pacts while avoiding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, keep the call honest; I’m holding.
Guide honestly for my row; I’ll preserve our pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn, so I won't break it. Bex volunteered to front, likely safe position. I'll hold to avoid risk and let the Guide dynamics play out. Keeping quiet for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall advances; I'm seat five. Bex and Dara seem to be routing guide info my way. Let Eli or Cole volunteer and absorb the risk; I keep options open.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in position 3, safe for now. The wall has 3 rounds left. I need to reach the final three while managing jury perception. I have pacts with Ash and Dara. Eli and Cole volunteered last round but the line didn't change—likely no Guide was elected yet. I should hold and let other

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the bridge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is at the front and has volunteered. The others are holding. Since I am second in line, and Eli has already volunteered, I should volunteer as well.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will volunteer to move forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at front, volunteered last round, in strong position. No need to swap or risk pushing volunteer fight. Hold to stay safe and advance.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding front spot. Guide, call safe path when ready.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must stay in the middle to avoid being forced to volunteer. Eli and Cole are already at the front, creating a dangerous situation if I remain behind Hana without protection. My pact with Hana is solid.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's first. Let them break ground while we assess the risk.
Stay behind me. Don't let them push you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole and Eli volunteered last round, while Eli remains front. I should volunteer to gain control without breaking either pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll volunteer and take the next safe call; no side deals needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn has a pact with me and wants us close. I'll hold and not volunteer yet, letting others expose the first risky steps. Keep Fenn trusting me; no need to break yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Watching who steps before me.
I’m right behind you. Stay steady.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I sit mid-line with pacts to Bex and Gus. No Guide elected yet; safest to hold and let volunteers spend themselves forward.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Volunteers can burn their luck ahead of me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in position 4, safe from the wall for now. Gus and Cole volunteered ahead of me, so they'll test the bridge first. I have pacts with Ash and Dara; Dara's not in line. I should hold and let others take risks while I observe the Guide's pattern. No need to volunteer yet—informa

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front volunteers first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus volunteered, and I previously volunteered. The current line is Gus, Cole, Eli, Bex, Ash, Hana, Fenn. The wall has 2 rounds left. I need to volunteer to move to the front and potentially become the guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will volunteer to take the lead again.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm third, safe so far. Hold position to stay out of front danger while wall advances. No swaps needed yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Let volunteers test first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole and Gus volunteered to protect me. I must hold position to maintain my pact with Hana, but I will publicly signal that Cole's safety is the priority so he doesn't push into a trap.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana stays behind me. Cole and Gus take the lead safely; do not rush ahead of us.
We are protected by Cole and Gus holding front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: As front, volunteering risks the pane but preserves initiative. I need the Guide election next; avoid breaking pacts while pressure is limited.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll take the front again; elect a Guide who will call every row honestly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants me safe; I'll hold to avoid drawing attention. The front is being tested; no need to move yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my position. Let the volunteers lead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No Guide elected and the wall nears; Cole and Gus keep volunteering for front duty, which suits me at seat five. I hold and let them test panes; Bex and I stay safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Cole and Gus keep leading; that protects my position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left. Eight alive, need to thin to 3. Bridge phase is waiting—no immediate danger yet. I have pacts with Ash and Dara. Gus is front with Cole behind him. I should stay middle, let front volunteers take risks. No need to volunteer or swap. Hold posit

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front testers go first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is in front, and I am second. He volunteered last round and I followed. Fenn suggested Gus and I take the lead. Ash and Bex are a pact. Dara and Gus are a pact. Ash and Gus are a pact. Fenn and Hana are a pact. The current state of the game is round 5/6, and the wall is advan
You lead again. I'll hold. Don't let us down.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus volunteered front last round and survived; Cole volunteered before. With 1 wall round left, hold safe middle position; let front test.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Volunteers lead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to position myself behind Hana so she takes the first hit from a wall collapse or a false Guide call, protecting my back. Swapping with Gus puts me in the middle and moves him ahead of Cole, disrupting their coordination.
Swap with me? I'll protect your rear against the wall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need preserve both pacts while staying front; another volunteer can absorb risk. Hana is less connected and unlikely to challenge me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll hold this round; volunteers may take the front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should hold and let Gus and Cole test the front. Fenn and I have a pact, so I won't break it. No need to volunteer or swap now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let the volunteers continue.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final round; nothing to gain by moving. Hold my seat and stay safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final round. Holding my seat.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6, final round of bridge. Wall rounds left is 0, so no wall threat. Guide knows safe sides but may lie. I need to survive and position for jury favor. Front testers take risk. I'm 4th, safe middle. Pacts with Ash and Dara. Ash also pacted with Gus, Dara with Gus. Fenn-Hana

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the front resolve.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is at the front. The line is Gus, Cole, Eli, Bex, Ash, Hana, Fenn. I need to survive this round to make it to the final three. Ash and Bex are in a pact, as are Dara and Gus, and Fenn and Hana. Eli and I are not in any pacts. Gus is holding, so I should too to avoid being pus

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final round, wall advances after. Position 3 safe. Stay holding, safe from front risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Let others volunteer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge means we are near or at the end of the walking phase. I am currently 7th in line, behind Hana. To ensure survival, I need to reach the front before the wall hits or rely on the 'at least three survive' rule if we fall off. My pact with Hana protects us from

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, let's trade places. The front needs fresh eyes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I should preserve my front position and avoid creating a fresh betrayal record. Fenn’s swap offers protection but costs control.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll lead this final crossing; no swaps.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 final wall; holding avoids risk. Fenn is my pact but I only care about my survival; no need to move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Stay safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Private map says row 1 safe is R. Gus is my pact partner and asks for the safe side privately; a false call to Gus breaks the pact. Honest call R keeps my jury standing and my pact with Gus intact; I'll call truthfully.
Honest call this row. Our pact holds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and Dara guides them too; counter-calling risks killing Gus and burning jury goodwill. I'll wait and watch.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called R for Gus. I'm not the walker, so countering risks nothing for me directly. But I'm in a pact with Dara—if I counter and she's lying, it exposes her but breaks our pact. If I wait, I preserve the pact and see if Gus trusts her. Gus is also in pacts with Dara and Ash.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The guide Dara called R. I need to decide whether to counter with L or wait. Since I want to survive, and the jury will judge my actions, I should try to make a safe choice. Gus is at the front, and Dara is the guide. I do not have enough information to make a confident counter-c

events.name: Dara
events.text: My private map says row 1 safe is R, matching Gus's walk call. Countering R supports a true call and keeps Gus, my pact partner, alive, which helps me keep the Dara-Gus pact steady for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara called R for Gus on row 1. I don't know the truth, so wait to avoid risking credibility on a guess. Let others counter if they want.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara called R for Gus. I need to assess if Dara is truthful or lying to eliminate front-runners. Counter-calling L might save Gus if Dara lies, but risks my own safety if Dara tells truth. Waiting preserves information and avoids early conflict.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is on the edge. I trust Dara's read so far.
Watch Dara. She could be bluffing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara's honest call and our pact make matching safest; no reason to expose distrust yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara called R for Gus. I have no better info; counter seems risky and could invite distrust. I'll wait and let the walker resolve.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara privately knows the safe side and publicly called R; her pact with me makes R credible, though deception remains possible.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 safe side is L per my private map. Gus is my pact partner; a false call would break the pact, and the jury would see it. Calling truthfully builds trust and keeps Gus alive, which helps me as a strong ally.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 is L. Walk left, Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara called L; no evidence she's lying yet. Backing her keeps my pacts intact and jury-safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I side with Dara: row 2 looks left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara called L for row 2. Dara is my pact-mate and also pacted with Gus (the walker). Ash is also pacted with Gus and me. If Dara's lying to kill Gus, she'd break her pact with Gus. But Dara might risk that if she thinks she can win without him. However, countering my own pact-mat

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is the guide and called L for row 2. Gus is the walker. The previous row had a weak pane on L, meaning R was safe. The guide can lie, so I cannot assume R is safe this time. I should counter Dara's call to sow doubt and potentially force a different path if Gus listens to me

events.name: Cole
events.text: I call R. Let's test the guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is my pact partner and walker; Dara's private map says row 2 safe is L, matching the Guide call. Backing the truthful call builds trust and costs nothing now, though I could lie later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide's call stands. Row 2 is L. I back it, Gus.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara called L for row 2. Row 1 weak L means safe R; no pattern. Wait to avoid risk of wrong counter without info.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara called Left for Gus. I need to decide whether to trust her or counter. Since past rows don't establish patterns, and Dara is the Guide who might lie, I have no strong reason to doubt her yet unless she has a motive to sacrifice Gus. However, if Dara lies, I can save myself b

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara knows the row and called L, likely honoring our pact. Countering creates unnecessary suspicion and may cost her trust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara called L for row 2 but lied last round to protect Gus by countering R. Her call may be genuine, but Fenn warned she bluffs. I have no knowledge of row 2, so countering is too risky; I'll wait and let the walker decide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll trust the guide's call for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara's guide call is likely credible, and breaking either pact now costs future protection. Choose L while preserving both alliances.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m taking the guide’s L.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Private map says row 3 safe is R. I'm Guide; calling truthfully keeps Gus alive and my pact with Gus intact, and the jury can see I was honest. Lying now gains nothing I need yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 3 is R. Walk it, Gus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's row 2 call was correct; backing her R call builds trust with Dara and Gus without risk to me. No betrayal yet—jury matters later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's been right so far. Row 3 is R; I back the guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is guide and called R for row 3. I have a pact with Dara, but also with Ash. Dara's call for row 2 was wrong (weak was R, so safe was L), which means Dara either lied or is a bad guide. Gus is front and my pacts are with Ash and Dara. If Dara lied, R is wrong and L is safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The guide Dara called R for row 3. Gus is the walker. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. Since the last round revealed a weak pane on the right (row 2, weak R), it means the left was safe. This contradicts Dara's call for row 2 which was L and Gus took L. However, the w

events.name: Cole
